caption:
The penny loafer is usually traced to a Norwegian slip-on, and became G.H. Bass's Weejun in 1936.

Analog Shift says an Esquire staffer saw the shoe in Palm Beach, and the editor Arnold Gingrich went looking for an American maker. Bass advertised the Weejun in the New York Herald Tribune on 27 May 1936 at $6.50. By the 1950s it was worn by American prep-school and college students. Why a penny went in the saddle is a matter of stories.

Connected to G.H. Bass, the moccasin, Esquire, Rogers Peet and the tassel loafer.
